text: . Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. India’s men’s and women’s teams have stormed into the finals of the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship being held in Ahmedabad.In the women’s semi-finals yesterday, India registered a convincing 39-14 victory over Sri Lanka, taking a commanding 24-7 lead at half-time. Uganda edged past Kenya 23-21 in the other semi-final.The women’s final between India and Uganda will be played at 7:30 PM Indian Standard Time today. The two teams will meet again following their group-stage encounter, in which India registered a 41-18 victory.Meanwhile, the Indian men’s team stormed into the final with a dominant 56-27 win over Bangladesh in the semi-finals. In the other semi-final, Sri Lanka defeated Kenya 28-24. The men’s final between India and Sri Lanka will take place at 9 PM today.

. In Men’s Cricket, India will take on New Zealand in the fourth T20 International of the five-match series at Eden Park in Auckland tomorrow. The match will begin at 12:30 PM.India have already clinched the series with a commanding 3-nil lead after winning the first three matches. India will now look to maintain their winning momentum in the fourth T20 International, while New Zealand will aim to bounce back.The fifth and final T20 International of the series will be played on Sunday.

. India has asserted that military solutions cannot resolve global challenges and that diplomacy must be given an opportunity to address conflicts. Speaking at the first plenary session of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, the United States, last night, External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar stressed the need to preserve freedom of navigation and ensure an end to attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers, in accordance with international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). His remarks come amid ongoing conflicts in different parts of the world, including the Russia-Ukraine war and escalating tensions in West Asia.Dr Jaishankar said that countries of the Global South are disproportionately bearing the consequences of attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers. He noted that such attacks are threatening the availability of essential commodities, including fuel, food and fertilisers, and driving up their costs. At least 22 Indians, including 14 seafarers, have lost their lives in West Asia since the conflict began in February this year.The External Affairs Minister, who reached Atlanta on Thursday, also held interactions with his counterparts from several countries ahead of the meeting.Dr Jaishankar will also participate in a QUAD Foreign Ministers’ Meeting with his counterparts from Japan, Australia and the United States on the sidelines of the G20 meeting. The United States is scheduled to host the G20 Leaders’ Summit in Miami on 14 and 15 December.Following his engagements in Atlanta, Dr Jaishankar is scheduled to travel to St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, to lead India’s delegation to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, scheduled from 1 to 4 November.

. India has called on the United Nations Human Rights Council to maintain sustained attention to the threat of terrorism, describing it as one of the gravest threats to human rights, particularly the right to life.Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations, Bhavika Mangalanandan, said terrorism continues to pose a serious challenge to the enjoyment of human rights.She noted that the Human Rights Council had recognised this threat in a resolution on international cooperation adopted in Geneva in July. The resolution called upon the international community to take necessary measures to strengthen cooperation in preventing and combating terrorism. India urged the Council to address the threat consistently, guided by the principle of zero tolerance towards terrorism.Ms Mangalanandan also criticised the Council for politicising and weaponising human rights issues and applying double standards. She cautioned that such practices undermine the Council’s credibility.

. Union Health and Chemicals and Fertilzers Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda administered the National Unity Day pledge to officials of both Ministries at a ceremony held in New Delhi.The observance commemorated the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and provided an occasion to renew the commitment to the ideals of unity, integrity and national cohesion. The pledge-taking ceremony reaffirmed the collective commitment of officers and officials to upholding the unity, integrity and security of the nation.National Unity Day, or Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, is observed every year on 31 October to honour the legacy of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and reiterate the importance of national unity and solidarity.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 30 paise to close at 94 rupees and 95 paise against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.67 in intra-day trade.

. India and Nepal have agreed to strengthen border security through better intelligence sharing, coordinated operations and the use of modern surveillance technology. The agreement was reached at the 10th Nepal-India Coordination Meeting between India’s Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) and Nepal’s Armed Police Force (APF), which concluded in Kathmandu today.The three-day meeting began on 28th of this month and was co-chaired by SSB Director General Sanjay Singhal and APF Inspector General Narayan Dutta Poudel.Both sides agreed to step up coordinated action against human trafficking, drug smuggling, counterfeit currency and other cross-border crimes. They also decided to strengthen checks and document verification at border points to prevent unauthorised entry of third-country nationals.A key focus was the adoption of smart border management systems. Discussions included installing CCTV cameras along sensitive border areas, baggage scanners and walk-through metal detectors at major checkpoints, and expanding the use of drones for surveillance.The two sides also agreed to work together to remove encroachments and unauthorised structures in the no-man’s-land area and improve the maintenance and reconstruction of border pillars.Cooperation in disaster response was another important focus, with discussions on organising a joint swift-water rescue exercise at Kurintar in Nepal. Both forces also agreed to expand training exchanges and strengthen institutional cooperation to counter misinformation and the misuse of social media.Both sides expressed satisfaction with the outcomes of the meeting and reiterated their commitment to strengthening coordination and cooperation to maintain peace, security and stability along the India-Nepal border. They also provisionally agreed to hold the 11th India-Nepal Coordination Meeting in New Delhi in 2027.

. In Gujarat, Women’s semi-finals of the Commonwealth Kabaddi competition concluded today with thrilling encounters. In the first match of the evening, Uganda edged past Kenya with a score of 23-21, while India dominated Sri Lanka 39-14 in the second match. With these results, India and Uganda have advanced to the final. The match will be played tomorrow at 7:30 PM. India currently holds the top rank in the women’s group.

. Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today highlighted that India’s civilizational consciousness will offer valuable guidance in dealing with present day challenges in the country. The Minister stated this at the book launch of Timeless India: Protection and Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the leadership of the Prime Minister in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat said that this book offers a unique perspective on the initiatives undertaken by the government to safeguard and revive India’s rich cultural heritage. He emphasised that preserving and revitalising this legacy is essential not only for safeguarding the country’s historical identity but also for shaping its future.This book is written by Former Rajya Sabha Member Tarun Vijay and  published by Indira Gandhi National Centre of Arts and Surbhi publication.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Jan Bhagidari.Jan Bhagidari, which means public participation, is a core governance model under Narendra Modi government. Schemes that utilize the Jan Bhagidari model include Swachh Bharat  Mission, Catch the Rain, Vocal for Local, and Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. Citizens in India had traditionally been treated as passive beneficiaries of government schemes. Jan Bhagidari has brought a change to this and fostered local ownership and behavioural change in people. Prime Minister Narendra Modi regularly highlights Jan Bhagidari as a core pillar of nation-building through his monthly radio program, Mann Ki Baat. In Mann Ki Baat  last month, Prime Minister Modi again highlighted Jan Bhagidari as a driving force for social change, urging citizens to join collective movements like the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan.Talking to Akashvani News, Shivendra Singh, a resident of Prayagraj, spoke about how he and his family and friends believe in Jan Bhagidari and go Vocal For Local during festive seasons.Participation has now become ownership of transformation happening around the country, with the people becoming stakeholders in national development.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has emphasised that country’s next phase of economic transformation must be driven by young entrepreneurs who look beyond the domestic market and aspire to build world-class brands. He said this while interacting with students at the Festival of Ideas, held in New Delhi today.Mr Goyal said that with an expanding start-up ecosystem, manufacturing capabilities, various free trade agreements and deeper integration with global value chains, country offers immense opportunities for young Indians to createglobally competitive enterprises and generate employment. The Minister also encouraged the youth to seize emerging opportunities across manufacturing, deep technology and high-value services with a strong export-oriented mindset,globally benchmarked quality, industry-relevant skills and the confidence to take calculated risks.

. In Men’s cricket, hosts New Zealand defeated India by 87 runs in the fourth T20 International at Eden Park in Auckland. Chasing a massive target of 260 runs, India managed to score 172 for nine in their allotted 20 overs. For the visitors, Tilak Varma top-scored with 35 runs, while Naman Dhir contributed 28. Jacob Duffy led the New Zealand bowling attack with four wickets, while captain Mitchell Santnera and Matthew Fisher claimed two wickets each.Earlier, put into bat first, New Zealand posted a massive 259 for seven, powered by spectacular centuries from Glenn Phillips, 107 runs off 49 balls and a quick-fire contribution from Michael Bracewell 65 off just 25 deliveries. New Zealand’s total was the highest T20 International score by any team against India. For India, Mayank Yadav claimed three wickets, while Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Axar Patel took one wicket each.Despite the defeat, India remain in control of the five-match series with an inaccessible 3-1 lead. The fifth and final T20 International will be played on Sunday.

. Manisha Bhanwala scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the Wrestling World Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan. She also became only the second Indian wrestler to claim a world championship title, after Sushil Kumar, who won the men’s 66-kilogram gold in 2010.Manisha clinched the women’s 59-kilogram gold with a remarkable 8-6 comeback victory over American wrestler Abigail Nette in the final. Trailing 0-6, Manisha staged a stunning recovery to secure the gold medal and end India’s long wait for a women’s world champion in wrestling. Manisha had stormed into the final with a dominant semifinal victory over Kazakhstan’s Altyn Shagayeva.Also, for the first time, three Indian women reached the gold medal bouts in the same edition of the World Championships. Neelam Sirohi in the 50-kilogram category and Kajal Dhochak in the 76-kilogram category won silver medals after losing their respective finals yesterday. Tanmu Sharma also secured a bronze medal.

. The India Meteorological Centre (IMD) has said that a well marked low pressure area over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal persisted over the region today.It is most likely to persist over the region and intensify into a depression today. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression tomorrow and into a cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday morning.Under the influence of likely formation of cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday and its further intensification, isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected  over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday and Wednesday and  further over Odisha and Telangana on Wednesday.IMD has issued red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow.The Met Department has forecast Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and South Interior Karnataka will experience heavy rainfall tomorrow. The weather agency has said that thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds is likely over East Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh tomorrow.

. The Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi organised an event titled ‘Six Yards of India – The Saree Story’ in collaboration with the General Women’s Union (GWU) and the Diplomatic Group for Spouses of Ambassadors at the GWU headquarters in Abu Dhabi.The event showcased India’s rich textile heritage and the cultural diversity reflected in its traditional sarees, bringing together Indian craftsmanship, fashion and art.The programme featured a presentation on the history and significance of Indian sarees by Ms. Reema Mahajan, Founder of the Indian Women Association, followed by a session titled ‘Threads of Tomorrow – India Fashion, Reimagined’ by fashion designer Mr. Kaushik Velendra.A Bharatanatyam demonstration by Ms Rashika Ojha added a cultural dimension to the evening. The programme also included a film and quiz on India, an exhibition of Indian art and an experience of Indian cuisine.The event highlighted the diversity of India’s traditional weaves, including Banarasi silk, Kanchipuram silk, Mysore silk, Kerala Kasavu, Bandhani, Kalamkari, Bengal’s Tant Saree as well as regional draping styles like Nauvari and Seedha Pallu, offering guests an insight into the country’s centuries-old textile traditions.

. The United States has approved a potential sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) interceptors to Ukraine at an estimated cost of 2.1 billion US dollars. The acquisition will be funded entirely by European partners and Canada, with no financial contribution from the United States.The US State Department formally announced the approval yesterday, stating that the proposed sale aims to strengthen Ukraine’s air defence capabilities and protect it against current and emerging missile threats.Canada, Germany and Norway are expected to contribute towards the purchase through the US JUMPSTART programme, along with financial support from a European Union credit facility. US defence company Lockheed Martin will serve as the primary contractor for the proposed deal.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has welcomed the US State Department’s approval of the procurement of Patriot missile interceptors to counter incoming Russian ballistic missile attacks. In a social media post, Mr Zelenskyy described the approval as a “strong decision”. He said the 500 PAC-3 interceptors would significantly strengthen Ukraine’s air defence capabilities and could provide an effective defence package during the winter months. However, he urged Washington to expedite their delivery in view of Ukraine’s immediate security needs during the winter season.Earlier this week, Mr Zelenskyy said that Kyiv had been waiting for nearly a month for formal approval from Washington for critical missile supplies intended for its Patriot and NASAMS air defence systems.

. The government has constituted a High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat to review the country’s banking sector and recommend reforms in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.The Finance Ministry said that the Committee will recommend structural, institutional, regulatory and legislative reforms to make the Indian banking sector globally competitive, financially inclusive and resilient. The Committee will be chaired by former Central Vigilance Commissioner Suresh N. Patel.Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu, former Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Indian Bank Padmaja Chunduru, and former RBI Deputy Governor N. S. Vishwanathan will be its members. The Joint Secretary (Banking) in the Department of Financial Services will serve as the Member Secretary. The Committee will have a tenure of six months. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had announced the setting up of the Committee in her Budget speech this year.The Committee will assess existing banking practices and prudential norms, identify global best practices and examine their suitability for adoption in the Indian banking system. It will also review the existing regulatory and legal frameworks governing banks, including Regional Rural Banks and Cooperative Banks, and suggest reforms to improve efficiency and ease of banking.In addition, the Committee will prepare a roadmap for the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital innovations in banking institutions, while recommending safeguards against cyber risks.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined over 1.2 billion US dollars to 719.7 billion US dollars during the week ended on 23rd of this month. According to the Reserve Bank of India’s data, Gold reserves dropped by 2.6 billion US dollars to 103 billion US dollars. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund fell four million to 4.78 billion US dollars.In contrast, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, rose 1.3 billion US dollars to 593.2 billion US dollars during the week. Special Drawing Rights grew by 27 million US dollars to 18.6 billion US dollars.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the deep depression over East central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has moved southeastwards and intensified into a Deep Depression today. IMD added that the deep depression is very likely to move nearly southwestwards, and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over east central adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal by early morning tomorrow. It has advised fishermen not to venture into West Central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days.The Weather Agency has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow. Heavy Rainfall is also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh during the next two days.The Met Department has predictedthunderstormsaccompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Gangetic West Bengal, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days.For Delhi, the IMD has forecast a clear sky tomorrow. The maximum temperature in the National Capital will be around 31 to 33 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature will hover around 15 to 17 degrees Celsius tomorrow.

. In Hockey, India continued their winning streak at Men’s Asian Champions Trophy by defeating China 5-2 in their second league match at Jalandhar in Punjab this evening.The Indian team maintained its momentum despite a strong attacking display by China.Earlier in the day, Malaysia defeated South Korea 3-1 in the first match of the tournament while Japan edged past Bangladesh 1-nil in the second match.Tomorrow, India will take on Japan, Bangladesh will face Malaysia, and South Korea will meet China.

. In Hockey, India defeated Japan by 4-1 in the ongoing Hero Asian Hockey Championship at Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar, Punjab. This is the third consecutive win of the host India in this championship.Meanwhile, in the first two matches of the day, Malaysia pounded Bangladesh by 6-1, while South Korea beat China by 2-1.

. The nation is remembering former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her death anniversary. Congress President and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge, senior party leader Sonia Gandhi, and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi paid tributes to Indira Gandhi at her memorial, Shakti Sthal, in New Delhi.In a social media post, Mr Kharge said that Indira Gandhi’s contributions to building a strong and progressive India remain an enduring legacy. He added that her supreme sacrifice for the unity and integrity of the nation would forever be etched in the collective memory.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during the next three days. According to IMD, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience heavy rainfall today.MetDepartment has also predicted thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds over East Rajasthan, Konkan, Goa, Lakshadweep, Madhya Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh today. Similar weather conditions are likely to prevail over Odisha, Rayalaseema, Telangana, Coastal Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka for the day.For Delhi, the Weather Agency has forecast a clear sky today.

. Prasar Bharati has brought laurels to India, with Nongmaithem Nandakumar Singh winning the prestigious ABU Broadcast Engineering Excellence Award 2026 for his outstanding contribution to broadcast technology and innovation.Among his notable innovations are DDPlayout, an indigenous automated playout software adopted by multiple Doordarshan Kendras, and DDSlowMo, a cost-effective slow-motion replay system used in national-level sporting events.The award was presented by the Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union, or ABU, a regional organisation bringing together around 224 broadcasting and media organisations across 66 countries.The 63rd ABU General Assembly and Associated Meetings are being held in Colombo from October 30 to November 3. The five-day gathering brings together broadcasters, media leaders, engineers and industry experts for technical, programme and sports group meetings, alongside the Broadcasting for All Forum, Media Leaders’ Forum and Super Panel.Held under the theme “Media for Peace and Humanity: Truth, Trust, and Transformation”, the assembly provides a platform to discuss innovation, emerging technologies and the future of broadcasting.The recognition of a Prasar Bharati engineer highlights India’s contribution to broadcast engineering excellence and technological innovation across the Asia-Pacific region.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reported a sharp acceleration in bank credit growth, alongside a decline in interest rates on fresh loans and deposits during the month of September this year.According to the RBI’s latest data, non-food bank credit grew 19.1 per cent year-on-year as of 30th September, compared to 11.2 per cent in the corresponding period last year. Credit to the services sector recorded the highest growth of 28.3 per cent, while agriculture and industry registered growth of 19.5 per cent each. Credit to the personal loans segment grew 17.3 per cent, compared to 11.5 per cent a year ago.The RBI data also shows that the weighted average lending rate on fresh rupee loans declined to 8.51 per cent in September from 8.61 per cent in August. The rate on outstanding loans remained unchanged at 8.96 per cent. Interest rates on fresh term deposits also eased to 5.61 per cent from 5.67 per cent.According to provisional data released by the RBI, country’s services exports increased over 39 billion US dollars in September this year, up 7.2 per cent year-on-year. Imports rose 12.6 per cent to over 20 billion US dollars, resulting in a services trade surplus of around 19.2 billion US dollars.

. Human rights activist Amjad Ayub Mirza has condemned the reported killing of five members of a family, including three children, in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). He has urged the United Nations, the Government of India and the international community to intervene amid allegations of escalating violence against civilians.In a press statement issued from Glasgow, Scotland today, Chairman of Jammu Kashmir Tehreek-e-Ittifaq-e-Rai Mr. Mirza said that a grenade or rocket attack on a civilian residence had killed three children, their mother and their grandmother.Calling for an impartial investigation, Mirza said the deaths of the children and their family members demanded accountability and international scrutiny. The appeal also cited allegations by senior Joint Awami Action Committee members Umer Nazir Kashmiri, Mujtaba Farooqi and Imtiaz Aslam, who have claimed that more than 100 young people have been killed, hundreds injured and thousands arrested or detained in PoJK since June 5. Mirza called for an independent international investigation into the reported deaths, protection for peaceful protesters, unrestricted humanitarian access, the release of those arbitrarily detained and disclosure of detainees’ whereabouts.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

. Most Asian stock indices declined today. South Korea’s Kospi dipped three and a half per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex index dropped two and a half per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 2.1 per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite slipped over 1.4 per cent, and Singapore’s Strait Times index lost nearly 0.4 per cent. In contrast, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose nearly one and a half per cent.Meanwhile, the Bank of Japan’s policy board voted 8-1 to keep its key short-term interest rate unchanged at 1.25 per cent. Board member Hajime Takata dissented, proposing an increase in the rate to 1.5 per cent. He argued that underlying consumer price inflation had reached the central bank’s price stability target and that the Bank of Japan should accelerate the pace of bringing interest rates closer to the neutral level.In European markets, Germany’s DAX dropped over half a per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 added 0.3 per cent, when reports last came in.Meanwhile, GDP of the European Union expanded by 1.5 percent year-on-year during the same period, up from 1.4 per cent in the previous quarter.

. In Hockey, India registered its third consecutive victory at the ongoing Men’s Asian Champions Trophy, defeating Japan 4-1 in Jalandhar, Punjab, last evening.India produced an impressive performance, with Abhishek Nain emerging as the star of the match. He scored two field goals and was adjudged Player of the Match. Vishnukant Singh scored one goal, while captain Harmanpreet Singh converted a penalty corner to score his fifth goal of the tournament. For Japan, Shota Yamada scored the lone goal through a penalty stroke. With this victory, India maintained its winning run in the tournament, having won all three matches so far.Today is a rest day. Tomorrow, November 1, India will take on Malaysia, South Korea will face Bangladesh, and China will look to open its account against Japan.

. Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said that a Marshall Islands-flagged LNG carrier M/T AL MAYEDA, carrying six Indian seafarers, was targeted yesterday in a projectile attack in the Persian Gulf.In a social media post, Mr Sonowal said that all six Indian nationals, along with the entire 25-member crew, are completely safe. He said India is continuously monitoring the situation and is in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and well-being of its seafarers.

. Indian shuttler PV Sindhu advanced to the women’s singles quarterfinals of the Hylo Open Super 500 badminton tournament in Germany today.The second-seeded Indian defeated France’s Pancasari 21-9, 21-6 in the Round of 16 to secure place in the last eight. Sindhu will next face Denmark’s Amalie Schulz in the quarterfinals.Meanwhile, Malvika Bansod and Isharani Baruah bowed out of the tournament after losing their respective Round of 16 matches.Bansod went down 11-21, 17-21 to Canada’s Wen Yu Zhang, while Baruah lost 14-21, 19-21 to Denmark’s Line Kjærsfeldt. In men’s singles, Lakshya Sen is set to face fellow Indian shuttler Kiran George in an all-Indian Round of 16 clash later this evening.

. In the United States, two Chinese nationals have each been sentenced to 30 months in prison for conducting covert intelligence activities targeting US military personnel.The US Justice Department said they were also sentenced to three years of supervised release for conspiring to act, and acting, as agents of the Chinese government without notifying the US Attorney General. According to the department, the two men operated under the direction of China’s Ministry of State Security. Their activities included arranging secret cash payments, gathering information about military installations and personnel, and attempting to recruit intelligence sources within the US military. Both defendants pleaded guilty to the charges.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

. India is hosting the BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise in Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The exercise is a key initiative announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Thailand.The exercise, which commenced yesterday, will continue until the 3rd of next month. It comprises three days of Tabletop Exercises, followed by a two-day Harbour Phase, with ships from BIMSTEC member countries participating.In a social media post, the Ministry of External Affairs said the exercise translates the shared vision of BIMSTEC leaders into action by reinforcing maritime cooperation, enhancing operational coordination and interoperability, and contributing towards a safe, secure and stable maritime environment in the Bay of Bengal.

. The Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak has been awarded to 490 police personnel from various States and Union Territories, Central Armed Police Forces and Central Police Organisations for 2026. The medal recognises outstanding work, promotes high professional standards and boosts the morale of police personnel.The Ministry of Home Affairs said the Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak was instituted on 1 February 2024. It is conferred on members of police forces, security organisations, Central Armed Police Forces, the National Security Guard, Assam Rifles and forensic science professionals.The medal recognises excellence in operations, outstanding service in investigations, exceptional performance, indomitable and daring intelligence service, and meritorious work by serving government scientists in the field of forensic science. It is announced on 31 October every year, on the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

. Indian wrestler Manisha advanced to the women’s 59 kg final at the World Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan today.Manisha defeated home favourite Altyn Shagayeva by a dominant 10-nil by fall to book her spot in the gold medal bout. She will face Abigail Nette of the United States in the final tomorrow

. The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards.It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it is likely to move further north and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh tonight.Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.An orange alert has been issued for very heavy rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is also expected in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.Thunderstorms accompanied by hail are likely over East Rajasthan, Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand and West Uttar Pradesh.Thunderstorms and gusty winds are also forecast in several other states, including Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam and Meghalaya.Meanwhile Delhi witnessed light to moderate rainfall this evening. The IMD has forecast very light rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning tomorrow morning.The maximum temperature is expected to remain between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to range from 16 to 18 degrees Celsius.

. Major US stock market indices ended lower yesterday. The Nasdaq Composite slipped 1.4 per cent, as investor sentiment was weighed down by corporate quarterly earnings and concerns over AI-related spending. The S&P 500 declined 0.3 per cent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost nearly 0.3 per cent.On the economic front, according to the advance estimate released by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), third-quarter GDP increased at an annual rate of 3.4 per cent, up from 2.2 per cent in the second quarter of this year.A separate report by the BEA showed that Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.6 per cent year on year in September, up from 3.4 per cent in August. Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 3.1 per cent, up from three per cent in August.

. The government has extended the existing customs duty exemption on cotton imports until the 31st of December this year. The Finance Ministry has issued a notification in this regard. The exemption, which was earlier valid until the 31st of October, has been extended to ensure adequate availability of cotton for the Indian textile sector.The extension is expected to reduce input costs across the textile and apparel industries, providing relief to manufacturers and consumers while safeguarding the interests of domestic farmers.The Finance Ministry said the measure is also expected to boost the performance of the domestic textile industry, particularly small and medium enterprises, by ensuring better availability of cotton in the market.

. Indian Railways has announced 1,265 vacancies for Station Master posts across various Railway Recruitment Boards and zones, opening up new employment opportunities for graduate candidates. The Railways Ministry said that in an important recruitment-related decision, the Railway Board has prescribed that Station Master recruitment will be notified separately from 2026 onwards. The dedicated recruitment process provides candidates with a specific notification covering eligibility requirements, examination procedures and vacancy distribution for the post. The online application window will remain open till 25th of next month. Candidates are advised to review the detailed eligibility conditions, vacancy distribution and application instructions before submitting their forms. The recruitment reflects Indian Railways’ continued efforts to provide career opportunities to eligible candidates while strengthening its operational workforce.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has announced a significant relaxation in the Know Your Customer (KYC) review rules for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to boost the ease of doing business. Under the new guidelines issued today, the market regulator has increased the periodicity of KYC reviews for various categories of FPIs.As per the new guidelines, for Category-One FPIs from non-high-risk jurisdictions and certain high-risk entities registered under specific regulations, the KYC review will now be required only once every eight years instead of the earlier shorter timeline. For other FPI categories, including regulated entities and non-high-risk Category-Two investors, the review period has also been rationalised to every eight years, while remaining at every two years for certain remaining entities.In another major relief aimed at reducing the compliance burden, SEBI has completely dispensed with the requirement for FPIs to intimate changes in information or submit a no-change declaration at the time of continuing their registration. FPIs wishing to continue their registration for a subsequent block of three years will now only need to pay the required fees to their Designated Depository Participants (DDP) at least 15 days prior to the expiry of their validity. The regulator said that the KYC review timelines for FPIs investing exclusively in Government Securities and SWAGAT-FI FPIs will remain unchanged. These new provisions are set to come into force with effect from 1st December of this year.

. Global crude oil prices rose over two per cent today amid geopolitical concerns. Brent crude was trading 2.7 per cent up at 117 US dollars and 97 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 2.4 per cent higher at 104 US dollars and 44 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated, dedicated to the nation and laid the foundation stone of various development projects worth over 400 crore rupees at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat. The projects include a sewage and water treatment plant, façade lighting, the upgradation of Narmada Ghat and the Rainforest, among others.Earlier today, on the second and final day of his visit to Gujarat, Prime Minister Modi paid floral tributes to the Iron Man of India, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, at the Statue of Unity in Ekta Nagar. Marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Patel, celebrated across the country as National Unity Day, the Prime Minister led the celebrations. In a spectacular aerial tribute, Indian Air Force helicopters showered flower petals over the world’s tallest statue.Later in the evening, the Prime Minister will participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations.Yesterday, Prime Minister Modi inaugurated ‘Bharat Parv 2026’ as part of the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations at Ekta Nagar. The festival, which will continue until the 15th of November, celebrates India’s cultural diversity, traditions, cuisines, crafts and heritage under the theme ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’. It brings together the cultural identities of States and Union Territories on a common platform.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar met EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, where they discussed ongoing global conflicts.Dr Jaishankar last spoke with Ms Kallas over the phone on 25 October to coordinate diplomatic positions and discuss global issues, including the conflict in the Gulf region.Meanwhile, in her remarks at the first plenary session of the G20 meeting, Ms Kallas highlighted the crises arising from the Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict in West Asia. Earlier, addressing the session, Dr Jaishankar reiterated India’s position on the importance of diplomacy in addressing global challenges.

. The nation is paying homage to the great freedom fighter Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary today. The day is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, or National Unity Day.President Droupadi Murmu and Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan paid floral tributes to Sardar Patel at his statue at Patel Chowk in New Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also paid tributes to the Iron Man of India, saying that Sardar Patel dedicated his life to building a strong, prosperous and capable India.Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj also paid floral tributes to the great national leader.Later, Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off the Run for Unity at the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium to mark Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Shah said Sardar Patel was a great personality who not only transformed the nation’s history but also shaped its geography. He added that India stands proudly on the global stage today because of the strong foundations laid by Sardar Patel.Popularly known as the Iron Man of India, Sardar Patel served as the country’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister. He played a historic role in integrating more than 560 princely states to build a united and strong India.Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrates his immense contribution to the political integration and unity of the country. The occasion also serves as a reminder of the importance of national unity, integrity, security and harmony in India’s diverse and vibrant society.Government institutions, schools and colleges are organising unity pledges, cultural programmes and awareness activities across the country to commemorate Sardar Patel’s ideals and legacy. The Run for Unity is also being organised at various places to spread the message of national integration, peace and brotherhood.

India will provide 430 electric motorbikes to field officers in Sri Lanka’s fisheries sector under a new Memorandum of Understanding signed between the two countries.The MoU was signed by Indian High Commissioner Santosh Jha and Sri Lankan Fisheries Ministry Secretary Dr. B.K. Kolita Kamal Jinadasa, in the presence of Minister of Fisheries Ramalingam Chandrasekar.Under the agreement, India will extend grant assistance worth 265 million Sri Lankan rupees to strengthen the mobility and operational efficiency of fisheries officials.The initiative will support faster field-level services and engagement with fishing communities, while promoting environmentally sustainable transport under Sri Lanka’s Clean Sri Lanka programme.The assistance reflects India’s continued commitment to people-centric development cooperation across Sri Lanka.

. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has successfully launched its next-generation navigation satellite, NVS-03, marking a significant step towards strengthening the country’s indigenous satellite navigation capabilities.The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18), carrying the satellite, lifted off from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, last night. It was the 20th flight of the GSLV. The satellite was successfully separated from the launch vehicle and placed in its intended Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit.NVS-03 is the third satellite in ISRO’s second-generation navigation satellite series. It is designed to ensure continuity and improve the availability of navigation services under the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), India’s indigenous regional navigation system.The satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock along with procured atomic clocks. It also introduces the L1 frequency band, in addition to the existing L5 and S bands, enhancing the capabilities of the navigation system. These advancements are expected to strengthen India’s independent positioning, navigation and timing capabilities for civilian, strategic and security applications.Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan has congratulated the entire ISRO team on the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission. In a social media post, he said the achievement would further strengthen NavIC and enhance the country’s satellite-based navigation capabilities. He added that the successful mission reflected India’s growing capabilities in space technology and its commitment to self-reliance in advanced technologies.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also congratulated the scientists, engineers and the entire ISRO team on the successful launch. In a social media post, he said the mission marked an important step towards strengthening NavIC, India’s indigenous satellite navigation system. He added that NVS-03, equipped with enhanced capabilities, would further strengthen the country’s navigation infrastructure and contribute to India’s vision of self-reliance in critical and advanced technologies.ISRO Chairman Dr V. Narayanan congratulated the scientists, engineers, industrial partners and academic institutions associated with the mission. Addressing the gathering after the launch, he said the satellite, weighing approximately 2,232 kilograms, had been precisely injected into its intended transfer orbit. He also highlighted that the mission was accomplished with a turnaround time of just 56 days between two successive GSLV missions, the shortest interval achieved so far.Speaking to the media, Dr Narayanan said ISRO had placed its third indigenous atomic clock in orbit aboard NVS-03, while two indigenous atomic clocks were already functioning in orbit. He added that the satellite had been launched as part of India’s Regional Navigation Satellite System, which aims to provide navigation services across the country and up to 1,500 kilometres beyond its borders.Explaining the programme, the ISRO Chairman said it envisages a constellation of seven satellites in orbit to provide these services. He added that NVS-03 was the fourth satellite launched under the programme and that signals from four satellites could be used for multiple purposes. He said the constellation would need to be completed before navigation services could be integrated with mobile systems for wider public use.
